# Telegram Bridge for DeepSeek Harness

Talk to DeepSeek Harness (DSH) from Telegram. The bridge runs a bot **inside the
DSH Host process**

eek Harness (DSH) from Telegram. The bridge runs a bot **inside the
DSH Host process** and lets you:

- **See every session** — titles, working directories, running/idle state, last activity.
- **Read r

esults** — the latest assistant answer, per-turn, with token usage.
- **Review a run** — the request

, the answer, every tool call (ok/failed with a
result preview), and the files it changed with `+/-`

counts.
- **Keep the agent working** — send plain text as a prompt, steer, stop a run,
create or re

name sessions.
- **Talk instead of typing** — Telegram voice notes are transcribed locally by
DSH's

voice-input model and sent as prompts.
- **Review media deliverables** — videos, audio, images and d

ocuments a turn
produced are sent to Telegram automatically; `/files` resends the last turn's.
- **A

nswer the human-in-the-loop moments** — approve/deny tool calls and answer
`ask_user_question` cards

from your phone when the desktop app is not in front
of you.
- **Get pushed the moment a turn ends*
* — with buttons for Result / Review / Status.

No inbound port, no webhook, no public URL: the plugin long-polls the Telegram
Bot API from the Host

## Setup
### 1. Create a bot and get a token

1. Open Telegram, talk to @BotFather, send `/newbot`.
2. Choose a name and a username (`…_bot`).
3.
Copy the token (`123456789:AA…`).
### 2. Give the token to DSH
Pick **one** of these (checked in this order):
| Method | How |
| Configuration | `botToken:` in the `telegram-bridge` row of the profile patch (not recommended for

shared machines). |
| Credential reference *(recommended)* | Set a `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` environment
variable for the user that launches DSH, or store it through the Harness credential store. The row
default is `tokenRef: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. |

For a Windows desktop install: **System Properties → Environment Variables →
User variables → New**,

name `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, value = the token; then fully
restart DeepSeek Harness (closing the wind

ow is not enough — quit from the tray
menu). The bridge reads the credential on startup.
### 3. Authorize your chat

1. After the restart, send `/start` to your bot. Because no chat is authorized
yet, the bot enters *

*pairing mode** and replies with your numeric **chat id**
and **user id** — nothing else is executed

.
2. Add your chat id to the plugin row in the **profile patch**
(`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\deskt

op\cordis.patch.yml` on Windows,
`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` elsewhere), not the bund

.yml` on Windows,
`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` elsewhere), not the bundle's own
patch:

(`allowedUserIds` works too for private chats; the two lists are merged.)
A row override replaces th

e whole `config`, so restate `tokenRef` when you
set `allowedChatIds`. The profile patch is reapplie

d after bundle layers, so
it survives plugin upgrades.
3. Restart DSH. Send `/help` — you should get

ers, so
it survives plugin upgrades.
3. Restart DSH. Send `/help` — you should get the command card.

> The bundle intentionally ships **no generated settings form**: it is a
> zero-dependency plugin th

at validates its own config and reports invalid values
> as warnings in the Host log. Configure it t

hrough the profile patch (or the
> bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` if you are developing it).

> Pairing never authorizes: an unknown chat only learns its own id, and the
> notice is rate-limited

. Until the id is in the allowlist, every command is
> ignored.
## Commands

Plain text (anything that does not start with `/`) is sent as a prompt to the
selected session — the
fastest way to keep an agent going from your phone.

Child-agent (**subagent**) and **archived** sessions are hidden from `/sessions`
by default. Set `se

ssions.includeSubagents: true` and/or
`sessions.includeArchived: true` to list them, or address one

directly with
`/use <full session id>`.
| Command | What it does |

| `/sessions` (or `/list`) | List sessions; tap a button to select one. |
| `/use <n \| id-prefix \|

title>` | Select a session by list number, id prefix, or title substring. |
[该节后续省略]
## Security model

- **Allowlist first.** Unauthorized chats can only learn their own ids.
- **No inbound listener.** L

ong polling means nothing is exposed on your network.
- **Authority matches DSH.** Claiming an appro

val or question only when
`auto`-unattended (or explicitly configured) is deliberate: granting tool

authority to a chat is a policy decision, and the timeout delegates back to
the in-app answerer.
- *

*Tokens never leave the Host.** They are resolved per startup, never logged,
never rendered into a m

essage, and redacted from diagnostics.
- **Everything is escaped.** User/model text is HTML-escaped

and chunked into
independently valid messages, so malformed model output cannot break delivery
or in

ject markup.
- **Callback data is short and scoped.** Session ids in buttons are validated
against l
ive sessions before use.
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Data comes from the Host's own services: `sessionController` (list, inspect,
prompt, cancel, create,

rename, projections), `sessionQuery` (titles),
`workspaceChanges` (per-turn changed files), `typert

Gateway` (desktop-client
presence), `webApp` (GUI URL), and `credentials` (token reference). Nothing

is
scraped from the filesystem and no session events are written.
## Limitations

- Text messages and voice notes inbound; outbound media is limited to the
Bot API's ~50 MB upload ce

iling and the `deliverables` allow-list. Oversized
video/audio is transcoded when ffmpeg is availabl

e; other oversized files are
skipped with a note.
- Inbound photos, documents and stickers are not r

ead yet.
- One bot token per installed profile; `apiBaseUrl` supports a self-hosted Bot API server.

- Telegram messages are edited best-effort: very old approval/question messages
may keep a stale key

board, but a late tap is rejected as expired.
- Only long polling, not webhooks.
- Deep links into t
he desktop app are not generated; `/whoami` shows the GUI URL.
